papers_read.title_as_printed: Elicited clinician knowledge did not improve dementia risk prediction in individuals with mild cognitive impairment (Wang et al., Journal of Clinical Epidemiology 2023)
Longitudinal multi-modal data prediction model for mild cognitive impairment by deep survival analysis (Zhang et al., BMC Med Inform Decis Mak 2026, article in press)

what_each_reports.P-742: Bayesian Cox models (informative expert priors vs non-informative) on 34 baseline clinical/biomarker predictors, 365 ADNI MCI, outcome time to all-cause dementia within 3 years (142 events); ten-fold cross-validated Harrell's c-index 0.74 (0.70-0.79) with expert priors, 0.75 non-informative, 0.72 frequentist; 0.74-0.77 in sensitivity analyses. No ROC analysis.
what_each_reports.P-353: tdCoxSNN on baseline demographics/APOE plus longitudinal neuropsychological tests (MMSE and CDRSB excluded) and 116 sMRI ROI measures, 922 ADNI MCI; 20% held-out test set; cumulative/dynamic AUC 0.9089 +/- 0.01 at t = 1 year after a 1-year landmark, AD conversion; performance declines at longer horizons.

quantity_a: Harrell's concordance index over a 3-year window for all-cause dementia, from baseline predictors, ADNI MCI, ten-fold cross-validation.
quantity_b: Cumulative/dynamic time-dependent AUC for AD conversion within 1 year after a 1-year landmark, from longitudinal predictors observed up to the landmark, ADNI MCI held-out test set.
incompatible_if_same: Not assessable as a contradiction: the two are single performance figures from different models, and neither paper claims an ordering the other refutes.

gates.task: match at T-level (T2 progression prediction), different horizon and outcome definition (3-year all-cause dementia vs 1-year AD after a landmark).
gates.validation_tier: match at V2 (internal only), different schemes (ten-fold CV vs held-out test split).
gates.modality_family: partial: P-742 baseline clinical predictors including binary CSF/FDG-PET positivity and hippocampal atrophy; P-353 longitudinal neuropsychological scores and sMRI ROI densities.

endpoint_and_metric: incompatible: Harrell's c-index (global concordance over follow-up) vs cumulative/dynamic AUC at a single short horizon; different endpoint (all-cause dementia vs AD) and different information set (baseline only vs longitudinal up to a landmark).
performance_validity: flag does not apply: neither figure meets the ceiling test; both n > 300.
independence: Shared cohort: both use ADNI MCI participants (non-independence recorded); no shared authors.
grounds: P-742 reports Harrell's c-index and performs no ROC analysis, while P-353 reports a cumulative/dynamic AUC at a 1-year horizon, so the metric types differ.
The endpoints differ (all-cause dementia within 3 years from baseline vs AD conversion within 1 year after a 1-year landmark), and P-353 notes that its discrimination falls as the horizon lengthens.
The information sets differ: P-742 uses baseline predictors only; P-353 feeds repeated neuropsychological and MRI measurements up to the landmark into the model.

evidence_quotes.quote: the predictive performance was evaluated using ten-fold cross-validation via c-index, integrated calibration index (ICI), and integrated brier score (IBS).
Our study outcome was the time to all-cause dementia over a 3-year period for participants with MCI at ADNI enrollment.
When expert knowledge was incorporated, the c-index, ICI, and IBS values were 0.74 (95% CI 0.70-0.79)
The predictive performance was evaluated using a test set at time intervals t =1, 2, 3, 4 years from the landmark time s = 1.
attaining cdAUC values of 0.9089±0.01 alongside BS of 0.1651±0.01 with t =1 year on the test set
Longitudinal variables from two modalities of biomarkers i.e. cognitive function and structural MRI morphometry were also analyzed.

record_defects: claim_a labels P-742's result 'AUC 0.74'; it is Harrell's c-index (the record's own text and g4_note say so).
P-353's 'AUC 0.91' is a cumulative/dynamic AUC at t = 1 year after a 1-year landmark; the record carries no horizon or landmark.
claim_a is truncated mid-sentence ('time to  on T2').
modality_family 'clinical_survey' mislabels both papers (P-353 uses sMRI ROI measures; P-742 includes CSF/FDG-PET positivity and hippocampal atrophy).
Status 'partially_resolved_candidate' with bridging papers P-764 and P-876 does not fit a record rejected for metric incommensurability; the bridging entries do not explain the pair.
what_would_change_the_verdict: Both models evaluated with the same metric, endpoint and horizon on a common ADNI split; neither paper provides this.
